text: Decision: standardise on pnpm as the package manager for every workspace in the repo. Yarn lockfiles must be removed.
Fix: CI was failing because the lockfile drifted between npm and pnpm. Resolution: delete package-lock.json and rerun pnpm install in CI.
Gotcha: pnpm does not hoist transitive dependencies by default. Code that relied on accidental transitive imports must add direct dependencies.
Morning everyone, hope you all had a good weekend. Coffee is on in the kitchen.
Decision: session tokens are stored only in HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax cookies, never in localStorage.

Fix: the CSRF token check rejected legitimate cross-origin requests from the docs subdomain. Resolution: add docs.example.com to the trusted origin list and require the X-CSRF-Token header for state-changing verbs only.
Reasoning: localStorage is XSS-exfiltratable; HttpOnly cookies are not. Therefore session tokens belong in HttpOnly cookies even though the SPA cannot read them directly.

Gotcha: SameSite=Strict cookies are not sent on the first cross-site click that lands on a protected page, so the initial request appears unauthenticated. SameSite=Lax is the working trade-off for login redirects.
Quick reminder: standup is moving to 10:30 starting next Monday. Calendar invites already updated.
Decision: large Postgres migrations must run with statement_timeout disabled in a dedicated migration session, not in the application connection pool.

Fix: a deadlock between background vacuum and an online ALTER TABLE caused the migration to hang for 14 minutes. Resolution: pin migrations to run during the autovacuum cool-down window and lock_timeout = '5s' so they bail fast instead of stalling.

Reasoning: building an index on a 50M row table without CONCURRENTLY takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and stalls all writers. Therefore every production index migration uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and a retry guard against duplicate index failures.
Gotcha: jsonb_set returns NULL when the target path does not exist unless create_missing is true. Calls that omit create_missing silently drop the write.
Lunch order for the Friday all-hands is going around the channel. Reply with your pick by 4pm Thursday.
Decision: backend services use tetis-logger for all logging. Pretty-printed in dev, JSON structured in prod, with automatic error serialization.

Fix: request bodies were being logged in full and leaked Stripe webhook signing secrets into the log aggregator. Resolution: install a redaction serializer on the logger that drops Authorization, X-Webhook-Secret, and any field named 'token' or 'password'.
Decision: public API versioning lives in the URL path (/v1, /v2). Breaking changes require a new path segment; additive changes stay on the current version.

Fix: a stale CDN cache served a deleted user's profile for ~12 hours after deletion. Resolution: set Cache-Control: private, no-store on every authenticated profile endpoint and add a purge step to the deletion job.
Reasoning: a global IP-based rate limit punishes shared NATs and CGNAT. Per-account token-bucket limits give the same DDoS protection without false-positives against legitimate office traffic.
Welcome to the new hires joining this sprint — feel free to introduce yourselves in the channel.

Gotcha: tsc --build with composite projects does not re-emit declaration files when only JSDoc changes. Use tsc --build --force after large doc-only refactors or downstream packages will see stale d.ts.
Decision: every package targets ES2022 with module=NodeNext and strict=true. No exceptions; opt-out PRs are rejected at review.

Fix: the Node container OOM-killed under load because the default --max-old-space-size of 1.5GB was lower than the container memory limit. Resolution: set NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 to match the 4GB pod limit with headroom.

Reasoning: committed .env files leak even after git rm because git history retains them. Therefore the only safe rotation after a leak is to rotate the credential at the provider, not to remove the file from main.
Anyone going to the JS conference next month? Putting together a group rate request.
Gotcha: enabling gzip on responses below ~1KB makes them larger, not smaller, because of the gzip framing overhead. Set a min-length threshold of 1024 bytes.
Decision: integration tests must hit a real database, not a mocked one. Reason: a prior migration broke production while mocked tests passed clean.

Fix: a flaky e2e test failed once a week because it asserted on Date.now() drift across the test runner and the server. Resolution: freeze the clock with vi.useFakeTimers() inside the test and seed the server with a fixed --now flag.

Reasoning: at-least-once delivery requires idempotent consumers, because the broker will retry on any uncertain ack. Therefore each consumer step persists a processed-idempotency-key before it commits side effects.
Anyone have a recommendation for a good mechanical keyboard for long coding sessions?
